text_blocks.snippet: Losartan is a prescription medication (commonly sold as Cozaar) used to treat high blood pressure, protect kidney function in type 2 diabetes, and reduce stroke risk.
Most common and mild side effects often improve as your body adjusts to the medication:

list.snippet: Dizziness, lightheadedness, or fatigue (especially when standing up quickly)
Upper respiratory infections (such as a stuffy or runny nose, sinus pain)
Digestive issues (mild nausea, diarrhea, or stomach upset)

text_blocks.snippet: Serious Side Effects (Seek Prompt or Emergency Care)
Contact your doctor or seek emergency medical help right away if you experience:

list.snippet: Allergic reaction / Angioedema: Sudden swelling of the face, lips, tongue, throat, or eyes, or trouble breathing or swallowing (this is a medical emergency).
High potassium levels (Hyperkalemia): Muscle weakness, confusion, or a slow, fast, or irregular heartbeat.
Kidney problems: A major decrease in how much urine you pass, or swelling in your hands, ankles, or feet.
Severely low blood pressure: Extreme dizziness, feeling faint, or passing out.

text_blocks.snippet: You can read more detailed prescribing guidance via the Mayo Clinic Losartan Guide or the Cleveland Clinic Losartan Overview.
